name: São Brás de Alportel
mandate: PrompTugal.news São Brás de Alportel: AI and technology in São Brás de Alportel, a hill town of cork heritage, a costume museum and a municipal push to digitise, and what reaches São Brás de Alportel from the Algarve, Portugal and the world. Independent; every fact sourced.

gravity.text: São Brás de Alportel is a small inland municipality whose identity rests on heritage (the Museu do Traje, the cork industry and now Praça 1914, an outdoor industrial heritage space) and on a manufacturing base led by Globalfire, a fire-detection technology maker that is described as its largest employer and exporter. Its AI story is early and public-sector led: the council is a partner in the intermunicipal Algarve 6.0 smart territory project, runs a coworking space and an entrepreneur's office, and backs research at the University of Algarve.

ai_news.title: Regional development body visits São Brás schools, including a specialised informatics centre
ai_news.summary: The vice-president for education of CCDR Algarve toured the town's school network on 4 November 2026. The secondary school has a specialised technology centre in informatics, described as the first of its kind in the region. The mayor said a 6 million euro school expansion still awaits an answer on its recovery-plan application. The report does not mention AI.

ai_news.ai_path: An informatics training centre is where local students would learn the skills AI work builds on. The council page does not say AI is taught.

ai_news.title: Council forum puts a local IT firm and a medical-technology firm on stage
ai_news.summary: At the sixth Fórum Ideias de Negócios on 27 October 2026, two panels presented local businesses. Among them were InovaPrime, an information technology company, and Savvy Alpha, working in medical equipment and technology. The council says it will follow the presented projects through the year. The report does not mention AI.

ai_news.title: Town hall and University of Algarve prepare a knowledge and innovation pact
ai_news.summary: The council and the University of Algarve met in April 2026 to widen their partnership into teaching, training and research, including school and business links through short higher-education courses. They agreed to work towards a pact in the coming months. The report does not mention AI.

ai_news.title: Council backs an AI workshop at the University of Algarve
ai_news.summary: The council supported a March 2024 workshop on deep learning for food quality sensing, co-organised by the university's electronics research centre and a European research network, with nine international experts and about 40 participants.
ai_news.ai_path: The workshop itself is about AI (deep learning), and the municipality funded part of it.

extras.label: Largest employer and exporter (not AI)
extras.value: Globalfire makes fire-detection technology in the Barracha industrial zone and exports to about 90 countries. The council page does not mention software or AI, so it is context, not an AI map entry.

extras.label: Praça 1914
extras.value: Joined the Rede Portuguesa de Turismo Industrial on 10 November 2026 (council news), described as the first outdoor site of the network on the mainland.

extras.label: São Brás ON
extras.value: The council's monthly feature on local business projects, run by the entrepreneurship office and published in both local newspapers. The page names no members and no AI focus.

extras.label: Storm Charles, 11 November 2026
extras.value: 21 incidents, mostly minor flooding and wall falls, coordinated from an operations centre. The council's account names no digital warning system or data platform, and mentions technology only in that the civil protection commission met in hybrid format.

extras.label: First year of the council's mandate
extras.value: The 2 November 2026 balance lists health, housing, education, safety and economic development as priorities, with a business park among the works. It does not mention digital, smart territory or AI.

extras.label: Starting a company here: first stop
extras.value: The council's Gabinete do Empreendedor receives founders and investors, clarifies the legal requirements, refers them to specialised partners (IAPMEI for small and medium firms, CRIA and microcredit agencies for founders, ACRAL for commerce, AHISA for hotels and restaurants, IN LOCO for artisans and local producers), helps publicise and reach financing programmes, follows the firm through municipal procedures and runs training sessions. The page sets out no step-by-step procedure. Its contact channel is on the same council page.

extras.label: Starting a company here: where to work
extras.value: Three municipal incubation spaces: a coworking space for young entrepreneurs, Ninho de Empreendedorismo 4 Olhos, and Ninho de Empreendedorismo da Vila (one office, three coworking desks, two spaces for digital nomads, a meeting room).

extras.label: Starting a company here: grants and events
extras.value: The Digital Commerce Accelerator offers help with applications for a non-repayable grant of up to 2,000 euros per company for shops, services and restaurants. The council's Fórum Ideias de Negócio is its yearly meeting point for new ideas and support services. The council lists three support measures (local businesses, entrepreneurship, employability) whose subpages have not been read.

extras.label: Nearest weather data
extras.value: Per the conductor's IPMA map (board/briefs/2026-11-16-storm-local-map.json), the nearest IPMA station is Olhão EPPO at about 15 km and the nearest forecast place is Loulé at about 12 km, so the town has no station of its own.

gaps: Third read of the council's entrepreneur showcase (all four pages): the clearly digital local businesses are We Stream Algarve, Substância3D (3D and streaming) and Peanuts (marketing and digital content). None mentions AI, so they are listed as leads at three steps, not as AI companies. Still no AI company, startup or lab found, and the commercial registry has not been read.

Lead firms: searches on 16 November 2026 for InovaPrime, Savvy Alpha and Aplitec (named on the council's forum page) found no website, product page or description we could read, so none can be called an AI user or builder. The next sources are the business registry and the firms' own pages if they exist.
The council's site shows no mention of AI in its front-page news and has no RSS feed we could find, so its news must be read page by page.

Postal do Algarve and Sul Informação blocked our automated reading with a bot check or an error, so their São Brás stories are not used here until they can be read openly. The pages with a bot challenge were skipped on purpose.

Sources to find next: the University of Algarve's electronics research centre for any town link, the business association for local digital firms, and the Algarve 6.0 platform's supplier and timetable.

The council's own November 2026 news (the first-year balance, Storm Charles, Praça 1914) never mentions AI or the Algarve 6.0 platform, so the municipal AI story is told by regional press, not by the council.

Investment map and local talent: no investor, investment or startup founded in the town is documented in the sources read. Local talent who have spoken publicly is not listed, because no public speaker profile has been found and the agent does not name private individuals.
The council's three support-measure subpages and the Via Verde para o desenvolvimento page returned no detail to our reader, so grants and fee waivers for investors are not stated.

Events: the whole council agenda (five pages, 15 November to 5 December 2026) is now read. It lists markets, concerts, reading clubs, sports, nature walks and film sessions, with one local entrepreneurship action at the Saturday market, and nothing about AI or technology.

Algarve 6.0 platform: a search listing points to a January 2026 EU tender by the Algarve intermunicipal body for a leased urban management platform, worth roughly 356,000 euros before VAT. We could not open the notice, so this is an unconfirmed lead. No supplier, award or timetable is known, and the project page on the national transparency portal returned an error.

InvestAlgarve: search listings say the regional investment support network opened a service point in São Brás de Alportel in November 2016, but we could not open those pages and found nothing newer. It is not known whether it still operates, so it is not on the map. The council's Gabinete do Empreendedor is the current first stop.

Council news list of 16 November 2026 (six items: boccia award, CCDR school visit, Storm Charles, EM 523 road, Praça 1914, scholarships) was read; only the school visit has a technology angle, none mentions AI.
The scholarship notice (6 November 2026) prioritises health students and does not mention technology or AI.
A search for AI news in the town in November 2026 found nothing new; results were the already-recorded EduTalks, Algarve 6.0 and University workshop stories.
A Postal do Algarve piece on Algarve digital and smart villages appeared in search but was not opened, so it is not used.

voice.gravity: São Brás is a small town up in the hills that lives on heritage, from the Museu do Traje to cork and now Praça 1914, with Globalfire, a fire-detection maker, as its biggest employer and exporter. The AI chapter is still being written, and the câmara is holding the pen: a smart territory project with its neighbours, a coworking desk, an entrepreneur's office and a hand for the university.
